newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities tumble further, end bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: German equities tumble further, end bourse lower.

text.p: German blue-chip DAX index fell nearly two percent over bourse dealings on Friday, tracking losses from electronic trade on Thursday and then continuing a downwards trend seen in recent days.

Low volumes and high volatility characterised trade over the session, which ended down 78.57 points, or 1.86 percent, at 4,188.28 points, while the September DAX future contract was down 33 points at 4,152.86 points.
"I wish I could tell you what's driving us down today. We're trending, and trending downwards, same as we've been seeing the whole week," a Frankfurt broker said.
A trader said: "Because of holidays in many parts of Europe volumes will be very low."
There was little market moving data around to help the DAX make a meaningful move in any direction, either towards a more significant correction or a new rally.

Dealers said that the focus continued on utility RWE AG, which on Wednesday night announced plans to shelve an unpopular system of multiple voting rights attached to shares held mainly by local municipalities.
The move was viewed as opening up the company to international investors, by loosening old ties on its equity.
Holders of preferred shares in RWE will be invited to swap these for common shares under the new voting rights system.
RWE common stock rose strongly in early bourse, but fell back to end the day down 30 pfennigs at 86.70 marks.
The Assumption holiday in the southern states of Germany also contributed to the listless session.
